builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: A.S.E 2.0: Understanding How Repository Context Impacts the Security of LLM-Generated Code
summary: The technique replaces default functionality-oriented context construction (standard retrieval, file ranking, agent-driven exploration) with security-aware context construction that explicitly surfaces safeguard code and excludes insecure exemplars before generation. It costs additional engineering to identify and annotate security-relevant repository elements per project, plus modest retrieval overhead, and provides no runtime latency change since it affects only context assembly. It can fail when safeguard locations are misidentified, when the model ignores injected safeguards, or when the security-relevant code is too dispersed across the repository to fit the context window.
rationale: The paper provides a benchmark and diagnostic findings rather than a validated production tool, so the reader should pilot safeguard-aware retrieval on their own security-sensitive codebases to confirm the effect transfers before committing to it as standard practice.
technique: Security-aware repository context construction for LLM code generation

claims.statement: The technique replaces default functionality-oriented context construction (standard retrieval, file ranking, agent-driven exploration) with security-aware context construction that explicitly surfaces safeguard code and excludes insecure exemplars before generation. It costs additional engineering to identify and annotate security-relevant repository elements per project, plus modest retrieval overhead, and provides no runtime latency change since it affects only context assembly. It can fail when safeguard locations are misidentified, when the model ignores injected safeguards, or when the security-relevant code is too dispersed across the repository to fit the context window.

Withholding a safeguard lowers the secure pass rate by up to 8.1 percentage points; one inserted insecure exemplar raises correct-but-exploitable code by 6.3 pp; functionality-oriented context raises functional pass rate up to 8.2 pp but secure pass rate by at most 3.7 pp; coding agents observe the relevant safeguard in only 27-36% of trajectories.
